chapter_title: Chương 291: 0293【Đầu tư cổ phần vào công ty game di động】

segments.title: Chương 291: 0293【Đầu tư cổ phần vào công ty game di động】
segments.content:
The gaming industry's attention on *Future Era* was something that happened after the Spring Festival.

Before the festival, on the 28th of the twelfth lunar month, Chen Guiliang flew back to his hometown.

After landing in Rongcheng, he planned to visit a game company.

At the ChinaJoy expo last summer, a bunch of founders from small and medium-sized game companies had hoped Chen Guiliang would invest in their games.

At the time, Chen Guiliang hadn't taken a fancy to any of them.

Now, another small company had been emailing Chen Guiliang for days, asking for help.

It was Chen Guiliang's public email address, a place where people with even a slightly closer relationship wouldn't send messages.

Due to the overwhelming amount of junk mail, he usually didn't check it himself. Instead, his assistant at Youke would screen it first, reporting anything deemed valuable and treating the rest as spam.

Of course, Chen Guiliang would also personally check it from time to time to prevent his assistant from doing anything foolish behind his back.

The game company asking Chen Guiliang for help was called Dingguo Technology.

They claimed to have developed a 3D mobile game engine based on the Symbian platform and had already created a 3D mobile game (a semi-finished product). But they had run out of money and were in a very difficult situation.

Youke was currently expanding into the mobile game market, and Chen Guiliang had already recruited an eight-person R&D team.

A small workshop had actually managed to create a 3D mobile game engine?

Curious, Chen Guiliang decided to check out the situation in person. Since he had to go home for the New Year anyway, stopping by on the way would only delay him by half a day at most.

"I've arrived. Where are you?" Chen Guiliang asked over the phone.

The person on the other end replied, "I've been at the main gate of the residential complex. I'm waving, President Chen, can you see me?"

"I see you," Chen Guiliang said.

A young man in his twenties, wearing a down jacket, was waving frantically at the entrance of the complex.

His name was Tang Kai, one of the founders of Dingguo Technology.

"Hello."

"President Chen, it's so great to see you. And this is?"

"This is my driver, Yang Shuo."

"Hello, Mr. Yang."

Tang Kai led them into the residential complex and soon arrived at a three-bedroom apartment. A sign reading "Dingguo Technology Company" was still hanging on the door.

Tang Kai opened the door and introduced, "Our company has seven people in total. We're all bosses, and we're all employees. We aspire to be the Blizzard of China, so none of us draw a salary. We've been at it for a year."

Running on passion.

All seven of them were bosses, which meant the equity was very diluted. It would easily lead to conflicts if the company grew.

But they obviously hadn't thought that far ahead, because they couldn't even afford to pay salaries. They were all just working for themselves for free.

Tang Kai said, "This three-bedroom apartment is both our company and our home. For a whole year, we've barely gone downstairs except to eat. We don't have fixed working hours either. Working more than ten hours a day is normal; we just crash when we're tired. The next day, we wake up and get right back to it."

Yang Shuo thought to himself: This is a group of madmen.

"Have you thought about how to sell the game?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tang Kai shook his head, "Let's finish the game first, then we'll take it to the big companies. We're working on two games simultaneously. One is called *Path of the Netherworld*, a 3D fantasy adventure mobile game. The other is called *Seven Nights*, a 3D horror mystery mobile game. We don't know which has a better market, so we're making both at the same time."

Chen Guiliang was speechless, but also impressed.

This showed that Chen Guiliang really wasn't familiar with the mobile game market in its wild, early days, because both *Path of the Netherworld* and *Seven Nights* were famous among early mobile gamers.

*Seven Nights*, in particular, would be nominated for "Best 3D Game" at the IMGA this year. Only five games worldwide were nominated for this award.

However, even sending just one person to attend would cost 6,300 euros for round-trip tickets and basic accommodation.

These seven young men couldn't afford it.

They posted on game forums asking for help, requested sponsorship from major domestic companies, and even emailed the IMGA organizers for assistance.

But the IMGA organizers didn't reply to their emails, no major domestic companies were willing to help, and the money crowdfunded by netizens on the forums wasn't enough.

So they had no choice but to give up on the award.

Both *Path of the Netherworld* and *Seven Nights* were well-received, with *Seven Nights* earning rave reviews. But what followed was rampant piracy; the official version couldn't sell at all.

With the piracy so widespread, a large company finally took notice of them, invested money, and had them develop a sequel to *Path of the Netherworld*.

The sequel finally made money, but the large company that invested in them embezzled every last bit of the revenue. And they refused to provide any further investment.

That large company was called "Huaxinfei," which meant "China's Chips Soar."

"The other six partners have all gone home for the New Year, so I'm the only one in the company right now." Tang Kai invited Chen Guiliang to sit on the sofa and went to make tea for him and Yang Shuo.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Did you start your own company to make games right after you graduated?"

Tang Kai said, "I graduated in '03 and joined a Japanese-funded company, developing games for the PS2 and Xbox platforms. Last year, I quit my job to make games and got six like-minded brothers to start a company with me. We're all young and haven't worked for many years, so our savings aren't much. We've almost used up all our savings now."

Chen Guiliang asked, "You guys didn't go to the ChinaJoy expo in the summer?"

Tang Kai said, "We had just started making the game back then and didn't have much of a product to show. There would've been nothing to do if we went, so we might as well have stayed in Rongcheng and saved on travel expenses."

"I'd like to see your game," Chen Guiliang said.

Tang Kai directly handed his phone to Chen Guiliang, first showing him the semi-finished *Path of the Netherworld*.

It was a 3D fantasy mobile game that could be played on all brands of phones, as long as the hardware could handle it. But if played on a Symbian model, the graphics could be better optimized.

To be honest, it was very crude, and the pixel count was very low.

Some monsters were just a blob, and it was impossible to tell what kind of creature they were.

But for a mobile phone in 2007, just being able to play a 3D game was good enough. What more could you ask for?

Chen Guiliang was now playing as a disciple from Mount Shu, searching for the fragments of three divine artifacts to seal the passages between the realms of Yin and Yang, and to prevent the sealed demons from reappearing in the human world.

If you got used to this crude, dark art style, it was actually quite engaging to play. The only thing was that the controls were a bit awkward at first.

Chen Guiliang never would have thought that he'd see the day he would play a fantasy mobile game using the physical buttons on a phone.

"You developed the 3D mobile game engine yourselves?" Chen Guiliang put down the phone.

Tang Kai nodded with considerable pride, "That's right. China's first 3D mobile game engine, and as far as I know, currently the only self-developed 3D mobile game engine in China."

Chen Guiliang asked again, "How much money have the seven of you invested in total?"

Tang Kai said, "About two or three hundred thousand yuan. Mainly for buying equipment, and then rent, utilities, food, and the cost of registering the company. Although we don't draw salaries, our meals are covered by the company. It's basically room and board."

Chen Guiliang fell silent again. An expenditure of two to three hundred thousand yuan had produced China's only self-developed 3D mobile game engine, and they were developing two mobile games at the same time. The team only had seven people.

Chen Guiliang said, "How are you thinking of collaborating? Investment or acquisition?"

"We'd like to retain some shares," Tang Kai said.

Chen Guiliang thought it over carefully. "Youke will invest 2 million yuan for a 60% stake in Dingguo Technology and will be responsible for selling your future games. I won't send people over to micromanage; you will continue to manage the company yourselves. After my investment, your salaries will be paid at a normal rate."

"I need to discuss it with the others," Tang Kai said.

Chen Guiliang smiled and nodded, "Of course."

Tang Kai walked into a bedroom with his phone. Before even closing the door, he said excitedly, "Old Ding, President Chen is at our company! President Chen... yes, the President Chen from Youke... right, he saw those emails I wrote asking for help..."

He called them one by one, got everyone online, and held a discussion in their QQ group.

Some thought selling 60% of the shares for 2 million yuan was too cheap, believing their game could be a huge hit. But after much discussion, they unanimously agreed.

Mainly because they were really running out of money. If they continued like this, they would probably have to ask their parents for money or take on outsourcing work for other companies.

Moreover, once Youke invested, they would no longer have to worry about selling the game.

If Chen Guiliang didn't step in, after they finished the game, they would only be able to post it foolishly on game forums, with no sales channels whatsoever.

What's more, Chen Guiliang promised not to interfere with the company's management.

After talking for a full twenty minutes, Tang Kai returned to the living room and said, "President Chen, we agree to this investment plan."

Chen Guiliang reminded him, "If these two games turn a profit, you can use your share to continue growing the company. If these two games can't turn a profit, then my subsequent investments will dilute the 40% of shares you hold."

"We are willing to take the risk," Tang Kai said.

Chen Guiliang stood up and said, "Alright then, let's settle on the intent to invest today. After the Spring Festival holiday ends, I'll send people over to sign the contract."

Tang Kai very enthusiastically saw him out of the residential complex.

The two of them hailed a taxi.

After getting in the car, Yang Shuo couldn't help but say, "They're working so hard to start their business. If the game doesn't sell, wouldn't it mean they did it all for nothing? And they sank all the money they earned from their previous jobs into it."

"They have dreams," Chen Guiliang said with a smile, "I like people who have dreams and are willing to chase them."

Tao Chenggang didn't count; that was a deliberately crafted persona.

But Chen Guiliang's investment in Tao Chenggang's *Reign of Hegemon* truly became a celebrated story in the gaming industry.

Tang Kai's repeated emails to Chen Guiliang asking for help were influenced by this story. He felt that if Chen Guiliang could invest in Tao Chenggang, he might also invest in him.

And it worked. It was a win-win for both parties.

These seven people were clearly masters at developing mobile games. If they could keep at it, the era of smartphones would be when they truly shone.

If Chen Guiliang were to give them some guidance then, they could really take off.

Chen Guiliang took out his phone and called Bian Guanyue. "Guanguan, I'm almost there."

Since he was passing through Rongcheng, he definitely had to visit Bian Guanyue's home, and also borrow a car to drive back to Longdu.

At this time in Rongcheng, there weren't even any car rental companies. That sort of thing only existed in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen.
